working_title: Why your battery doesn't die while you drive
hook: Why doesn't your car battery go flat while you drive?
body: Because a belt from the engine spins a small generator called the alternator. Inside, a spinning rotor carries an electromagnet. Its moving magnetic field sweeps past copper coils in the stator and pushes current through them. That current flips direction constantly, so a set of diodes turns it into one-way current the battery can store. A regulator keeps the voltage near fourteen volts, whether you idle or cruise.
engineer_note_draft: As an engineer, what surprises me is how much power such a small part makes from a rubber belt.
loop_line: So next time you start the engine, remember why your battery stays alive.
